verdict.rationale: Azure's own RBAC docs describe it as a fine-grained access management system on Resource Manager, and give a scoping example (one user manages VMs in a subscription, another manages virtual networks). That supports the core of least-privilege expressibility. The pack says nothing about condition-based policies or how policies are evaluated, so the story is only partly covered. Missing for 10: documented conditional policies (attribute-based conditions), explicit resource-level scope hierarchy documentation, documented policy evaluation logic (allow/deny precedence), independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a security engineer, least privilege is expressible — fine-grained IAM policies with conditions, resource-level scoping, and documented policy evaluation

citations.quote: Azure RBAC is an authorization system built on Azure Resource Manager that provides fine-grained access management to Azure resources.
Allow one user to manage virtual machines in a subscription and another user to manage virtual networks
